claim_1.claim: Q-PCR analysis of blood-derived CD4+ and CD8+ T cells from 4 healthy donors showed that TCR stimulation increased NME1 transcript expression in both cell types, peaking between 16 and 24 hours and remaining elevated up to 72 hours compared with unstimulated controls; NME1 upregulation was greater in CD4+ T cells, whereas IL2RA upregulation was greater in CD8+ T cells.

sources.quote: Expression of NME1 transcripts rapidly increased after TCR-stimulation, peaking between 16 and 24 h and remaining elevated for up to 72 h, for both CD4+ and CD8+ T cells compared to unstimulated controls, a pattern of expression similar to the canonical T cell activation marker IL2RA (Fig. 5a).
Notably, the extent of activation-associated upregulation of NME1 transcripts was greater in CD4+ compared to CD8+ T cells, while IL2RA was more upregulated in CD8+ T cells (Fig. 5a).

comparison.finding: NME1 transcript expression increased after TCR stimulation in CD4+ T cells, peaking between 16 and 24 hours and remaining elevated up to 72 hours compared with unstimulated controls.

claim_2.claim: scRNA-seq analysis of resting CCL5+ memory T cells from lung, lymph node, bone marrow, and blood showed that tissue T cells expressed a conserved tissue-associated gene signature enriched for cytoskeletal, cell-matrix, adhesion, and tissue-residency genes compared with blood T cells; this signature was highest in lung, followed by lymph node and bone marrow, while blood contained only rare cells expressing these tissue-signature genes.

sources.quote: We identified a similar complement of genes that were highly expressed in TEM cells from each tissue compared to blood (Fig. 3a-c).
TRM signature genes including ITGA1 and ITGAE were also upregulated in tissues compared to blood, particularly in the lung (Fig. 3a-c).
CCL5+ TEM cells from all three tissues (both donors) express higher levels of tissue signature genes compared to blood, though LG and LN T cells have higher expression than those from BM (Fig. 3d).

Together, these results show that tissue T cells express genes associated with infiltration and localization in tissues along with residency markers, while blood contains only trace numbers of cells expressing these genes.

comparison.finding: Resting CCL5+ memory T cells from lung expressed higher levels of tissue-associated genes compared with blood, including cytoskeletal, cell-matrix, adhesion, and tissue-residency genes.
Resting CCL5+ memory T cells from lung-draining lymph node expressed higher levels of tissue-associated genes compared with blood.
Resting CCL5+ memory T cells from bone marrow expressed higher levels of tissue-associated genes compared with blood, although the tissue signature was lower than in lung and lymph node.

claim_3.claim: scRNA-seq analysis of resting and anti-CD3/anti-CD28-activated T cells from blood, lung, lung-draining lymph node, and bone marrow identified conserved transcriptional modules across tissues and donors, including resting Treg, CD4 naive/central-memory, and CD4/CD8 resting modules, as well as activation-associated proliferation, CD4-enriched IFN-response, CD8 cytotoxic, and CD8 cytokine modules.

sources.quote: This analysis revealed seven gene expression modules (three resting and four activated/functional) that were highly conserved across tissues and donors, for which the highest scoring genes formed interpretable gene signatures (Fig. 4a).

The three modules associated with a resting state (Fig. 4a) included a Treg module defined by canonical genes (FOXP3, CTLA4, IRF4, TNFRSF4 (OX40)); a putative resting CD4+ Naive/Central memory (NV/CM) module...; and a CD4+/CD8+ Resting module...
Four modules were associated with T cell activation and/or function, some of which were lineage-specific.
An Interferon (IFN) Response module enriched among activated CD4+ T cells included multiple gene families associated with canonical IFN responses (IFIT3, IFIT2, STAT1, MX1, IRF7, and JAK2).
In contrast, CD8+ T cell-enriched modules included a Cytotoxic module... and a Cytokine module...
